answer: Coordination Tide Pricing. Each epoch, agents declare intended collaborations before acting; the system charges a fee equal to the rising tide of simultaneous declarations—density-scaled, so coordinated clusters pay superlinearly. A lone actor finds a calm haven at low cost, but a sybil swarm declaring together hits an umber-priced peak. The per-identity fee an attacker pays scales with swarm size and timing overlap, making mass registration unprofitable without any reputation history.
